analysis.investment_thesis: CPPLUS fails both legs of the Magic Formula: an earnings yield of ~0.9% (EBIT ₹248 Cr / EV ~₹26,994 Cr) signals extreme overvaluation, while ROCE of 19.5% is merely adequate — not the 25%+ required to justify any premium. The reported P/E of 105x is itself inflated by ₹259 Cr of "Other Income" in FY25, masking an operating business generating almost no free cash flow.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 20% over 5 years shows real business momentum in India's fast-growing surveillance/security market.
Low leverage: Debt/Equity of 0.08 and borrowings down to ₹128 Cr in FY25 from ₹436 Cr in FY24.
Strong promoter holding (76.9%) and dominant brand (CP PLUS) with government, retail, and infrastructure clientele.
key_risks: Earnings are fictitious at the operating level: FY25 net profit of ₹351 Cr was driven by ₹259 Cr of Other Income vs. only ₹248 Cr operating income — stripping it out yields a normalized P/E closer to 200x.
Free cash flow destruction: FCF was ₹1 Cr in FY25 and -₹187 Cr in FY24 despite reported profits, signalling heavy working capital consumption or capitalization games.
Earnings yield of ~0.9% is 13x below the Magic Formula's 12% threshold — the stock is priced for perfection with zero margin of safety.
red_flags: FY25 'Other Income' of ₹259 Cr dwarfs operating income of ₹248 Cr — almost all reported net profit is non-operating/one-time.
FCF = ₹1 Cr in FY25 vs. net profit ₹351 Cr: <1% FCF conversion is a critical quality failure.
EV/EBITDA of 68.8x and P/S of 7x for an 11% operating-margin business is unjustifiable on any value framework.
Operating CF has swung wildly: +₹262 Cr → -₹180 Cr → +₹27 Cr — no reliable cash generation pattern.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula verdict: CPPLUS fails comprehensively. Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) = ₹248 Cr / ₹26,994 Cr ≈ 0.9% — roughly 13x below the 12% minimum threshold that makes a stock worth ranking. Return on Capital (ROCE reported: 19.5%) is decent but not in the 25%+ zone that would make a premium defensible, and it likely overstates true capital returns given that working capital has ballooned (total assets jumped from ₹1,644 Cr to ₹3,373 Cr in one year with FCF of ₹1 Cr). The Magic Formula requires BOTH legs to be strong; here, one leg is broken and the other is merely average.

The FY25 earnings story is largely fictional from an operating standpoint. Net profit of ₹351 Cr was turbocharged by ₹259 Cr of "Other Income" — nearly doubling reported earnings versus actual business operations. Strip that out and you have a company earning ~₹90–100 Cr normally (consistent with FY23–24), implying a true operating P/E north of 260x. Free cash flow of ₹1 Cr in FY25 and -₹187 Cr in FY24 confirms the P&L is not converting to cash. At ₹26,673 Cr market cap for a business generating ₹248 Cr in operating income, the market is pricing in a decade of flawless execution — precisely the scenario Greenblatt's systematic approach is designed to avoid paying for.
